newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-LEHMAN OPENS UP FOUR-SHOT LEAD AT TOUR CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LEHMAN OPENS UP FOUR-SHOT LEAD AT TOUR CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Tom Lehman, gunning for two major end-of-season awards, shot a sparkling three-under 67 in blustery conditions Friday to seize a four-shot lead after 36 holes of the Tour Championship at Southern Hills.
British Open champion Lehman stood at seven-under 133, with Vijay Singh of Fiji alone in second place in the $3 million tournament at 137 after a one-over 71.
Steve Stricker was the only other player under par after 36 holes, his 68 Friday leaving him at two under par.
Lehman's 67 was low round of the day as 30 mile-per-hour (50 kph) winds made the course play 30 strokes harder for the field comprised of the tour's top 30 money winners.
"It was very difficult out there. I feel fortunate to have played so well," Lehman said. "You know when the wind is this difficult that a birdie really makes a statement."
After the turn Lehman went from a statement to full oration, posting birdies from the 10th through 13th holes, then tapping in for a fifth birdie on the 15th.
"When conditions are this tough it is sometimes easier to focus on that cliche 'one shot at a time.' You're just trying to survive each shot."

Should Lehman win this tournament he will lock up two important awards -- the PGA Player of the Year and the Vardon Trophy for low scoring average. He may also, depending on how Phil Mickelson finishes, take over the money title as well.
Singh finished with a bogey to widen Lehman's lead to four strokes.

Said Singh, "I was trying not to lose too many shots to Tom. I don't think any amount of lead is enough on this golf course, but if Tom keeps playing this well it's going to be very tough for the rest of us."
Red-hot Tiger Woods, distracted by the hospital admission of his father in the early morning hours on Friday, fell out of contention after soaring to an eight-over-par 78.
Woods spent half the night at a local hospital after his father, Earl, was admitted shortly after 2:00 a.m.

According to a Woods family statement, Earl Woods, 64, is being kept at Saint Francis Hospital under observation for a problem related to the bronchitis he developed earlier this week. Woods underwent quadruple bypass heart surgery 10 years ago.
"I didn't want to be here today, because there are more important things in life than golf," Woods said after his round.
"I love my father to death and I wouldn't want to see anything happen to him. Hopefully he's okay."
